items.title: The Street Fighter 2 Bonus Stage Car Is Real and You Can Win It
items.description: The General is teaming up with Capcom to bring the destroyable car from Street Fighter II to life, and you have a chance to win it — along with more than $25,000 in gas money.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The General is teaming up with Capcom to bring the destroyable car from Street Fighter II to life, and you have a chance to win it — along with more than $25,000 in gas money.

Street Fighter II’s iconic bonus stage lets players beat the literal brakes off of a Lexus LS 400. It’s a feature that’s stayed with the series throughout the years, challenging fighting game fans to beat it to a pulp within a certain time limit.

It’s even referenced in the upcoming Street Fighter movie, with trailers showing Noah Centineo’s Ken Masters punching and kicking a car to bits while surrounded by a crowd of adoring fans.

More than 30 years later, this car is coming to the real world, thanks to a joint collaboration between The General Insurance (yes, that General), Capcom, and Vehicle Effects, a Los Angeles-based company that makes custom rides of all sorts, many of which have been featured in films and TV shows.

Vehicle Effects has made a recreation of the pixelated Lexus from Street Fighter II — though we don’t recommend you actually destroy it if you end up winning it in their sweepstakes. Starting in October, fans have until November 18 to enter the sweepstakes for a chance at snagging the car for themselves, as well as $25,400.69 (nice) in gas money.

And hey, it’s a pretty good car; as pointed out by Eventhubs, the Lexus LS 400 is widely considered to be one of the most “overengineered” cars of all time, with a 4.0-liter V8 engine that’s been nicknamed the "million-mile engine.” (It’s the only thing left behind after you destroy it in the bonus stage, after all.)

On top of its pixelated paint job and upgraded sound system, the words “you” and “win” are emblazoned on both the driver’s side and passenger side headrests, and you can even insert a literal coin to activate its accompanying seat warmers. It’s hard to kick butt when you’ve got cold glutes, after all.

The Street Fighter movie releases in theaters on October 16, 2026. Just today, it was revealed that the movie will feature animated segments diving into Ryu and Ken’s backstory with their master, Gouken, and Akuma. We got the chance to speak to the cast of the film ahead of time, including David Dastmachian, who told us all about how he studied real-life cult leaders to bring M. Bison to the big screen.

Image Credits: Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures

items.title: Marvel Comics Reveals New Captain Marvel Series and Daredevil #700 - NYCC 2026
items.description: Marvel dropped some big announcements at NYCC, including Daredevil #700 and a brand-new Captain Marvel series from Kamala Khan co-creator G. Willow Wilson.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
Marvel Comics made some big announcements during the publisher's "Bullpen Bulletins! With Stephen Wacker" panel. The newly minted editor-in-chief revealed several big projects for early 2027, including a brand-new ongoing Captain Marvel series and the milestone issue Daredevil #700.

The new volume of Captain Marvel will be written by G. Willow Wilson, whom Marvel fans will best remember as the co-creator of current Ms. Marvel Kamala Khan. This time, Wilson is turning her attention to Kamala's mentor, Carol Danvers, who is facing a dark new status quo following the destructive events of Avengers: Armageddon.

Captain Marvel will be illustrated by Rachael Stott (Fantastic Four). Here's the official summary for the series:

Following the cataclysmic events of Avengers: Armageddon, Carol Danvers finds herself grounded like never before. To rise again, Carol will have to challenge everything she thought she knew about being Captain Marvel—and break every rule along the way. And as she pushes herself further, a threat that has been quietly assembling in the shadows of the Marvel Universe for decades is finally ready to make its move.

Look for Captain Marvel #1 to debut in May 2027.

As for Daredevil, the series will reach its 700th issue in March 2027. That oversized issue will feature a main story by regular series writer Stephanie Phillips and artist Lee Garbett, along with a new cover by Daredevil veteran David Mack.

Also during the panel, Marvel teased the climactic finale of a major Uncanny X-Men storyline called "Soul Deep," as well as a spinoff miniseries called X-Men: Regulators. Regulators is written by Mikki Kendall and drawn by Georges Jeanty and will debut in February 2027. You can see covers for these and the other books featured in the panel below:

Stay tuned to IGN all weekend for plenty more news from NYCC.

For more, see our exclusive first look at Mattel's first DC Premium figure and learn more about Timothy Zahn's surprise Star Trek debut.

items.title: Bill Murray Is a Ghostbuster Once Again... in a Car Ad
items.description: Bill Murray has reprised the role of Dr. Peter Venkman in a new advertisement for Rivian electric vehicles that sees the original Ghostbuster respond to a call of Slimer terrorizing a suburban house by pulling up in the "Ecto-R1," aka a Rivian R1S SUV decked out like the original Ecto-1 ambulance/hearse.
items.author: Ryan McCaffrey
items.content:
Bill Murray has reprised the role of Dr. Peter Venkman in a new advertisement for Rivian electric vehicles that sees the original Ghostbuster respond to a call of Slimer terrorizing a suburban house by pulling up in the "Ecto-R1," aka a Rivian R1S SUV decked out like the original Ecto-1 ambulance/hearse.

The 70-second spot shows off the special new Ghostbusters-themed Halloween software update for the R1S, R1T pickup truck, and new R2 SUV. In it, Rivian owners can play with a Ghostbusters UI on the cars' main center touchscreen display, play "'Mallow Mash" on the screen by squashing the Mini-Pufts flying around, plus hidden Easter eggs to discover. The update also adds custom sounds, a Slimer settings theme, a Trick or Treat Mode that can detect and greet costumed guests with Ghostbusters sound effects and lights, and custom themes for the exterior light bars, cabin lights, and overhead lights such as Proton Pack and Ghost Trap.

The Ghostbusters Halloween theme will be available in Rivians from today through November 2. Rivian launched its highly anticipated R2 earlier this year to great reviews. It keeps a very similiar design as the lauded R1S but shrinks both the size and the price. The R2's base price is $45,000, though in this current early stage of production, only the maxed-out, tri-motor, fully loaded Performance model is available for a starting price of $58,000.

Murray last played Dr. Venkman in 2024's Ghosbusters: Frozen Empire, which IGN's reviewer did not care for. The last Ghostbusters video game was 2022's Ghostbusters, Spirits Unleashed, an asymmetrical multiplayer game our reviewer thought was OK.

items.title: Lucasfilm Games Producer Responds After Galactic Racer Character Biddy Blas Goes Viral
items.description: If you’ve been on gaming Twitter recently, you’ve probably seen a clip from Star Wars: Galactic Racer making the rounds on your timeline — specifically, a player’s interaction with a character named Biddy Blas.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
If you’ve been on gaming Twitter recently, you’ve probably seen a clip from Star Wars: Galactic Racer making the rounds on your timeline — specifically, a player’s interaction with a character named Biddy Blas.

It’s almost impossible to hate the guy, who tells you all about how awesome he is in a hilarious spiel that has somehow become everyone’s new vocal stim. In Huttese, Blas tells you: “Here’s a name for you, amateur! Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!”

However, it’s the fantastic voice acting behind this line that’s got players cracking up. “Biddy Blas! Scrib doon!” is an undeniable banger, and I personally cannot stop saying it in response to basically anything. (My poor friend group is already tired of it.)

This Star Wars: Galactic Racer voice acting though! 💀🤣 https://t.co/oYkTMT2nSf

— NIB (@nib95_) October 6, 2026

Posts of Blas introducing himself have gone viral on social media, to the point where they caught the attention of Lucasfilm Games Producer Craig Derrick, who responded to the overwhelming influx of love for Blas on Twitter/X.

“It’s amazing to see so many people loving Galactic Racer!” he wrote. “Thank you for all the kind words! Every one of my social feeds is filled with posts about the game… while the algorithm continues to properly prioritize Mister Biddy Blas. I love it.”

Biddy Blas is a Crocin who, as players have come to find out, will literally do whatever it takes to win… even if that means giving you a ‘gift’ that’s actually a bomb, which, if you accept it, will explode your ship and give your opponents a major head start.

It’s amazing to see so many people loving Galactic Racer! Thank you for all the kind words! 🙏

Every one of my social feeds is filled with posts about the game… while the algorithm continues to properly prioritize Mister Biddy Blas. I love it. 😂 https://t.co/SdXjIq9HkF

— Craig Derrick (@craigderrick) October 7, 2026

Hate him or love him, the guy’s the talk of the town right now, with some fans affectionately dubbing him the “glup shitto of the year.”

“I would like to say I'd die for Biddy Blas, but at the same time, I have also slammed him into a wall at like 500mph multiple times at this stage,” one fan joked.

“Biddy Blas is hilarious, I'm going to kill him,” another said after their speeder got blown up thanks to accepting Blas’s ‘gift.’

Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been a major hit with Star Wars fans and critics alike, with IGN’s Luke Reilly scoring the game an 8 out of 10. “Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a fabulous looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer that gets a little repetitive thanks to its heavy reliance on repeatedly revisiting the same slim selection of planets, but has successfully lit the afterburners on a long-dormant slice of the Star Wars universe,” he wrote in our review.

It’s a good time to be a pod racer, as developer Fuse Games recently announced that Galactic Racer’s multiplayer party limit will soon double in size in a post-launch patch coming in the next few weeks.

items.title: Skate Developer Promises More Creative Tools Are Coming After ReSkate Modding Platform Goes Viral
items.description: Full Circle, the developer of Skate, published a statement addressing community mods following the viral launch of a fan-made modding platform called ReSkate.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Full Circle, the developer of Skate, published a statement addressing community mods following the viral launch of a fan-made modding platform called ReSkate.

ReSkate was officially released into the wild about a week ago. This platform allows fans to play the game offline, create private servers, make their own maps, and more. It’s already been downloaded over 350,000 times on GitHub, and its creators are well-aware that they might get hit with a cease-and-desist order.

However, that doesn’t seem to be a problem — at least, not yet, but the devs at Full Circle are keeping an eye on the situation. Full Circle published a statement acknowledging fan mods on October 9, where they admitted to the importance of community mods, while also standing firm against those that bypass paid cosmetics or make money off of new features.

“Skateboarding in general is built on community and creative expression, and we support that. We love seeing your passion for pushing the limits of San Vansterdam in different ways. That's why we built our new skateboarding sandbox in San Vansterdam to begin with, to give you, the players, the tools you need to have fun and create amazing content,” it wrote.

“To be completely clear, we are not against creativity from players or stopping that from happening. Where we have to draw the line is when mods or other tools bypass our systems to unlock paid cosmetics, release gated/unreleased content, or profit from these unauthorized assets. That rips off the artists, skate brands, and creators, as well as our own development team here at Full Circle, who work hard to bring skate culture into our game."

Full Circle went on to confirm that it is aware that players want “more freedom and custom features,” and revealed that it’s currently building “official, secure access tools that enable broader, deeper community creation.” More news on this will be shared at a later date.

A message from the team at Full Circle regarding mods and community content. https://t.co/sTiTUvkRWX

— skate. (@skate) October 9, 2026

ReSkate’s popularity is undeniable; after its release, Skate’s playerbase saw a massive jump in active players, peaking at over 7,000 players on October 5 — the highest it’s been for months after the game's launch in September 2025.

Speaking with PC Gamer, the developers of ReSkate admitted that they “honestly didn't realize how big this was going to be," saying they were “just doing it for the love of the game."

They also told the outlet that they are prepared to take ReSkate down if EA’s lawyers come knocking, which many fans are already assuming will happen at some point down the line. For now, though, ReSkate remains alive and well, and it has seemingly spurred Full Circle into taking action to give the game more community-friendly features.

items.title: Pretty Little Liars Star Keegan Allen Says He Was Robbed at Gunpoint in Bloody Video
items.description: Keegan Allen, best known for his role as Toby Cavanaugh in Pretty Little Liars, uploaded a shocking video to Instagram on the night of October 8, showing himself breathless and covered in blood.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Keegan Allen, known for his role as Toby Cavanaugh in Pretty Little Liars, uploaded a shocking video to Instagram on the night of October 8, showing himself breathless and covered in blood.

“I was just robbed of my watch outside of Laurel Supply,” Allen said, before turning away from the camera to ask someone to call the police. “These two dudes hit me in the head and pointed a gun at me, with a knife. They had masks on. They took my watch.”

Allen inserted CCTV footage from the incident taken by a nearby camera, which showed two men dressed in dark clothing approaching the actor near a truck. After Allen handed over his watch, one of the men struck him in the head twice, with both thieves quickly fleeing the scene.

In the caption of his Instagram post, Allen urged Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and California Governor Gavin Newsom to take action as the state's general election approaches.

“West Hollywood is not safe anymore,” he wrote. “Robbed at gunpoint and knifepoint by two young men that threatened to KILL me over my watch and would have! God said [not] tonight. My life for a watch. Will update more soon. Let’s hope all these flock cameras that @karenbassla @gavinnewsom and everyone thinks will stop crime can find these very dangerous criminals. God bless.”

The Los Angeles County Sheriff's office published a statement about the crime that recounted the attack: "One suspect pointed a silver handgun at the victim while the other pointed a knife and demanded the victim's watch and bracelet. Shortly after, the victim was struck in the face with the handgun."

The crime took place at Laurel Supply, a high-end organic grocery store and market on 8445 Santa Monica Blvd. Thus far, no arrests have been made, and individuals with information about the incident are encouraged to contact authorities at the sheriff's West Hollywood station at (310) 855-8850.

Allen’s bloody video has gone viral, racking up over 135,000 likes in the hours since he posted it last night. Fans are showing up in droves to give their support to the actor, urging him to get checked for a possible concussion and many admitting to initially being mistaken that he was wearing makeup for a new project.

Allen is also known for portraying Liam Walker in the CW’s Walker, a reimagining of Chuck Norris’s Walker, Texas Ranger. Most recently, Allen played Ian Coleman in Season 8 of The Rookie.

items.title: Comic Book Icon Grant Morrison to Pen New James Bond Series for IDW Publishing
items.description: In what may well be the biggest comic book news out of NYCC, Grant Morrison has been tapped to write a new James Bond series for IDW Publishing.
items.author: Jesse Schedeen
items.content:
In what may well be the biggest comic book-related news to come out of NYCC 2026, IDW Publishing has acquired the rights to publish new James Bond adventures. The company is turning to none other than legendary New X-Men and Doom Patrol writer Grant Morrison to launch a new ongoing James Bond series.

Few other details are known about the series right now, including the artist, official title, or release date. However, Morrison's name alone is ample cause for excitement.

We do know that Morrison's series will kick off with a six-part storyline dubbed "Sunbreaker." The writer teased their plans for the series in the following statement:

I’ve been a James Bond fan for as long as I can remember and this opportunity to put my own stamp on a British character as iconic as King Arthur, Robin Hood or Sherlock Holmes, was too good to miss.
Our opening 6-part adventure, Sunbreaker, attempts to create a definitive Bond story featuring everything fans love about the character and his world, while adding a whole lot more. Expect to see James Bond in a few unfamiliar situations, facing unfamiliar foes, in a world very like our own as reflected in a deadly funhouse mirror – a world of intrigue, violence, double cross and deception. A world through which James Bond glides like a killer shark among minnows. Charismatic, ruthless, unstoppable.
With new cars, new gadgets, and a terrifying new ultimate villain ripped straight from the headlines, get ready to be shaken and stirred, as James Bond faces the greatest challenge of his life in Sunbreaker!

items.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Launch Rollout Adds DMZ Early Access
items.description: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added DMZ to its list of early access experiences available for pre-order players ahead of its launch later this month.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has added DMZ to its list of early access experiences available for pre-order players ahead of its launch later this month.

Activision and Infinity Ward revealed a host of new details for its DMZ revamp in a blog post shared today. Early access for the mode joins campaign early access, with both available to those who pre-ordered either the standard or Vault Edition versions of the game across PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and/or Xbox Series X/S.

Here's the full breakdown: Eligible players will gain early access to the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 campaign starting Friday, October 16. DMZ early access will then follow Tuesday, October 20, with the full launch unleashing the rest of the experience come Friday, October 23. All of the new details arrived with a new gameplay trailer for DMZ, which you can see below.

DMZ was first introduced as Call of Duty's take on the extraction shooter experience with 2022's Modern Warfare 2. It was expanded upon in the months that followed but was ultimately deemed to be an underwhelming prototype by many. Support ended in late 2023, and now, Activision is taking another swing at it.

The DMZ in Modern Warfare 4 has been propped up as a fully fleshed-out evolution for the game mode. In today's post, Infinity Ward described the new take on the mode as the series' "definitive extraction shooter experience," promising persistent progression in the open-world combat environment known as the Hajin Exclusion Zone.

"There's an interesting story with the DMZ beta, where we had to make some decisions," studio multiplayer creative director Joe Cecot said in a recent behind-the-scenes video (below). "Certain things we wanted to do, we couldn't do. At the end of the day, we learned a lot: That we made a very approachable, fun sandbox that was fun to fight in, to explore, to make friends in, to get into fights in. There's a bunch of stuff we left on the table, so as soon as we finished with the last game, we were just gung-ho on, 'OK, we know what we want to do.'"

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 launches October 23 for PC and consoles. Our first proper look at DMZ gameplay arrived in June, with even more details shared earlier this week. While early access players will get to dive into DMZ and the story mode a few days earlier than others, core multiplayer offerings won't officially launch until that firm release date hits. You can see how the team at Infinity Ward is working to deal with wall-hack cheaters here.

items.title: New Avatar Show in Development as Seven Havens Renewed for Seasons 3 and 4
items.description: A brand-new show in the Avatar: The Last Airbender universe is in the works, focusing on an Avatar from the water tribe named Kuruk.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
A brand-new show in the Avatar: The Last Airbender universe is in the works, focusing on an Avatar from the water tribe named Kuruk.

The show is titled Avatar Kuruk: Wave of Chaos and takes place three generations before Avatar Aang. Avatar co-creators Bryan Konietzko and Michael Dante DiMartino are listed as showrunners, with Avatar Studios and Nickelodeon Animation Studios handling production.

As reported by Variety, the show’s logline is as follows: “A rebellious teenage Avatar bucks thousands of years of tradition by choosing to learn the four elements through globetrotting adventures, staying one step ahead of his angry teacher, rowdy pirates, and chaotic spirits – all while helping the world in his own unique ways.”

Paramount also shared a few first-look images at Avatar Kuruk at New York Comic Con, which show Kurk waterbending, taking in a view of the Northern Water Tribe Capital, and an image of his koala-like animal companion, Nikik.

Taking a shot at recent online leaks about the project during the NYCC panel, Konietzko said it will be the franchise’s first action-comedy. The panel also pulled back the curtain on the Avatar shows' production process, showing fans a special “script to screen” clip that was a visual explainer on how a scene of the series moves from the printed page to finished animation. The clip is now available on YouTube for all Avatar fans to enjoy.

Fighting game fans got their own moment. Varney unveiled new Seven Havens colorways for the full playable roster of Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game, along with a new stage based on Sonam’s temple.

This news coincides with Avatar: Seven Havens getting renewed for two additional seasons, bringing the total to four. The first three episodes in season one premiered today, October 9, on Paramount+, and three episodes will air weekly every Friday through October 30. At the time of writing, Book 2 does not yet have an official release date.

IGN's Alex Zalben reviewed the first three episodes of Seven Havens Book 1, which he scored a sparkling 9 out of 10. "The first three episodes of the new Avatar are thrillingly emotional, beautifully animated, and stunningly scored. It’s great to have this world back, even if it is a broken post-apocalyptic version that’s perhaps not too far from our own," he wrote in our review.

items.title: Dungeons & Dragons Is Going to Outer Space With Star Wars: Tyro Squadron, First Look at Official Art
items.description: Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft isn't even out yet, but Wizards of the Coast has already announced its next Universes Beyond release for the TTRPG – and it's Star Wars.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Dungeons & Dragons: World of Warcraft isn't even out yet, but Wizards of the Coast has already announced its next Universes Beyond release for the TTRPG – and it's Star Wars.

WotC announced that something Star Wars was coming to D&D back at Gen Con in July, but at NYCC 2026, it confirmed a new adventure, Star Wars: Tyro Squadron, along with a new Core Rules expansion for the Galaxy Far, Far Away.

The new Core Rules will likely be as large in scope as the recent World of Warcraft expansion, with a ton of story hooks and new ways to play classic D&D classes, but we don't know anything specific. WotC did reveal some information about the Tyro Squadron adventure module, however, but even then, there's not much there.

According to Wizards of the Coast, Tyro Squadron will let players "take the fight to the Empire as part of a secret Rebel crew. Set during the Original Trilogy, these new stories unfold as Luke and Leia fight their own battles across the galaxy. Fly daring missions, explore new corners of the galaxy, and help shape the Rebellion’s story."

Just like with Star Wars: Zero Company earlier this year, this new D&D campaign sounds like it focuses on the seedy underbelly of the Star Wars universe, rather than the bombastic heroics of Luke & Co.

Star Wars seems like a strange partnership for Dungeons & Dragons, and it's going to be interesting to see how the team works things like blasters and lightsabers into the traditional high-fantasy TTRPG. But, with how well the team handled the World of Warcraft expansion, this new partnership has at least piqued my interest.

Unfortunately, it seems like we'll have to wait a bit to know exactly what Wizards has in store for its Star Wars partnership. It said it will share more information about the expansion at Star Wars Celebration in April 2027.

items.title: Wardogs Dev Explains Why Blue Team Loses More, Confirms Plan to Address the Balance in Season 2
items.description: The team behind Wardogs has confirmed that Lonestar, AKA the blue team, loses more than other teams and is making big changes in Season 2 to fix that.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The team behind Wardogs has confirmed that Lonestar, AKA the blue team, loses more than other team, and is making big changes in Season 2 to fix that.

Since Wardogs launched in early September, there have been no shortage of memes mocking the game's blue team, Lonestar. For whatever reason, Lonestar tends to lose a lot, and there are a plethora of videos showing Lonestar players crashing helicopters at base and making fools of themselves.

Speaking exclusively with IGN, Bulkhead confirmed that Lonestar's win percentage is lower than other teams in Wardogs, but it has actually increased over time. Lonestar's win rate was roughly 10% during the game's alpha, but has risen to 20% in recent weeks. Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott noted that this is partially a result of players choosing to support Lonestar because they see it as an underdog challenge. He even joked that blue team's reputation was a bit of a PR issue.

"So originally, and this is key to not misquote, it was like 10% in the alpha," he said. "So that then led to the perception: blue is bad, don't join blue. And then everyone tries to click on green and click on red because they're competitive and they want to win. So they're going on the better team. More recently, it's closer to 15 to 20%. It's probably closer to 20% right now, where people have actively been joining blue team to try and make them win, which is quite entertaining to watch. But it's undeniable, they are losing more than the other two teams because of that perception."

Bulkhead is taking steps to remedy this with the launch of Season 2 next week. The biggest change is that they are adjusting spawns and rebuilding bases for all teams on the map Bakurani. Senior producer Kane Allard noted that blue team's reputation may have been compounded by the fact that they were losing significantly more on Bakurani, possibly due to map issues. As a result, they've chosen to shake up all of the spawns.

"We've moved all three spawns, so it's not just blue team have moved," said Allard. "It's blue, red, and green. They've all moved. The actual hot zone of Bakurani hasn't been changed. It's just the spawn zones. It's kind of revitalized the map, and we've seen from a data standpoint with our internal tests that it has evened it out. But yeah, as Howard said, there is a genuine PR issue with Lonestar, and there are a few extra things that we're going to be doing to hopefully help turn the tide of that, as well."

Some of those "few extra things" include changing the saturation on Lonestar's uniforms so they can blend in better, cash and XP bonuses for playing and winning as Lonestar, and even posters in the other teams' spawns encouraging other players to switch to blue team.

"Yeah, we are doing some fun stuff," said Philpott. "We're even putting posters like 'Lonestar needs you,' in the other teams' spawns. So yeah, it should be good fun."

In a press conference, Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer joked that, "if you're not playing blue team, you are in fact, a pu**y." So with that said, it is now up to the players to take these buffs and changes to try and change the perception of Lonestar.

Wardogs Season 2 launches on October 15.

items.title: Wardogs Dev Holding Back Certain Features Because of Xbox Series S, but Working to 'Very Low-End Hardware' Has Its Benefits
items.description: The developer of Wardogs has admitted that the limitations of the Xbox Series S have stopped it from adding certain things to the game, but insisted these limits have also provided some unique benefits.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The developer of Wardogs has admitted that the limitations of the Xbox Series S have stopped it from adding certain things to the game, but insisted these limits have also provided some unique benefits.

During a press conference for Wardogs Season 2, Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer said the team is "limited" by the Xbox Series S and revealed that this is one of the reasons why the game doesn't have dynamic weather right now. The new rain feature being added to Wardogs this month will be persistent throughout a match, meaning a storm won't suddenly roll through halfway through a game and lighten up within 15 minutes. It's a constant downpour.

"We are limited, as every dev is, by Xbox Series S," said Brammer. "As great a platform as Xbox is, it's a very low-end hardware for a game like Wardogs. We have to be mindful of these things we're putting in the game now. Performance is the reason we don't do it, but we would love to see it at some point. There's an ambition for it, but nobody is working on it right now."

Bulkhead isn't the first team to acknowledge difficulties around Microsoft's cheaper console, which launched alongside the Xbox Series X in November 2020. Moon Studio founder Thomas Mahler stated earlier this year that it was delaying No Rest for the Wicked's Xbox release due to troubles with the Xbox Series S. Baldur's Gate 3 also came to Xbox a few months late and required the help of Microsoft's engineers to get the game's split-screen co-op working on Series S.

Indeed, one of the questions facing Microsoft ever since the release of the Xbox Series S is whether it would be willing to allow developers and publishers to release a game on Xbox Series X only, leaving Xbox Series S behind. As it stands, Xbox mandates that video games launch on both or none at all, and that there should be main feature parity between each version.

Although Wardogs isn't coming to console until 2028, Bulkhead is hyper-aware of how everything it puts in the game could impact consoles in the future. In a follow-up interview exclusive to IGN, studio co-founder Howard Philpott echoed sentiments about possibly adding dynamic weather in the future, but noted Bulkhea would have to handle it carefully to avoid tanking performance. He added that, while Series S has its pitfalls, it also lets the developer optimize the game for lower-end PCs.

"As for Series S, Joe is right, and it's not an industry secret or anything," he said. "It is holding back what developers can do in terms of pushing the boundaries because it's so far behind par in terms of the rest of the power of the rest of the consoles. So yeah, it's something we have to be cognizant of, but at the same time, Series S does actually give us that baseline performance.

"We were so heavy [during] pre-release in terms of talking about performance for PC, and what we didn't necessarily talk about [during the] press conference was how much Series S drove us to make the performance good on lower-spec PCs, because the goal is to get everyone to be able to play with all of their friends. There's an obvious financial benefit to that, so it's not completely altruistic, but at the same time, it is the goal. That is the point of the game: being able to play with as many people as possible."

Philpott also noted that Bulkhead has always imagined Wardogs as a multi-platform game. The team recognized there was heavy demand for controller support prior to Wardogs' early access launch, prompting them to quickly put something together. He stated that this support is in "an okay serviceable state, but really it needs to be a lot better." Senior producer Kane Allard noted that situation has prompted Bulkhead to be more "forward thinking."

"I think that's a good example of one of the things that bit us a bit and made us realize actually we do need to be forward thinking," said Allard. "We made the decision, as Howard said, originally we were releasing on PC for early access, and it was kind of an afterthough, we need to have controller support. And then we realized there was a massive outcry for it, and we had to look back at the systems we had and try and make them work with controller, and there was a fair amount of work there. And yeah, we did do it in the end and it was a little bit of a slog, but that did burn us a bit. And we then realized, yeah, we need to be really smart, build stuff with console in mind, with controller in mind, and we're taking that forward for everything that we put in the game."

It will be a while before Wardogs makes its way to consoles, but this is a major part of the game's journey. Philpott also said that Bulkhead hired a pro Halo player to help with controller support and ensuring that it gets an extra level of care.

Wardogs Season 2 will launch next week on October 15.

items.title: Wardogs Dev Says PS6 and Xbox Project Helix Ports Should Be Relatively Straightforward
items.description: The team behind Wardogs expects to bring the game to next-gen consoles in the future.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
The team behind Wardogs expects to bring the game to next-gen consoles in the future.

Although some would argue that this console generation has yet to meet its full potential, platform holders are already ramping up for the next one with Sony's PlayStation 6 and Xbox's Project Helix, though neither company has locked in an official release window. However, it does mean some developers have to start planning ahead, and one of those studios is Bulkhead, the team behind the new shooter Wardogs.

In an exclusive interview with IGN, we talked about plans for the game's eventual console release. Wardogs is currently slated to make the jump to consoles in 2028, which begs the question: Will it release on next-gen hardware? Bulkhead says it's not even really a question.

"I think there's not too much to consider," said Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott. "We make the game performant, we're going to get it on the next-gen consoles. From our perspective, it's a straight port. So yeah, absolutely is the short answer, to be honest."

Senior producer Kane Allard noted that Bulkhead is already speaking with platform holders about the console versions of Wardogs, and doesn't anticipate any issues bringing the game to next-gen machines.

"We're obviously already in conversation with the proprietors of those platforms, and they're going to have certain criteria that we have to match, and I assume it's going to be the same for those other consoles as well. So from our perspective, if we get it on a base Xbox or base PlayStation, it shouldn't be much more work to get it on next-gen, and it should just be more performance. So I don't think it gives us anything new."

Last month, former PlayStation Worldwide Studios boss Shuhei Yoshida said Sony and Nintendo should make their current consoles last as long as possible amid soaring costs that have already prompted PS5 and Switch 2 price rises. Yoshida told The Verge that console companies needed to focus on sustaining their current hardware platforms for "as long as possible."

We know that a PS6 is on the way at some point. Previously, analysts had suggested a 2028 launch seemed likely, though Sony is yet to make any official indication of when PS6 may arrive — and as time goes on, that late 2028 release date feels less and less likely.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has insisted Project Helix remains part of Microsoft's gaming plan, but has also said next-gen Xbox hardware will be a "family of devices." "We are moving to a family of devices for Gen-10," she said in a memo reported by Windows Central. "There is not one device that fits all. We will certainly have a great console first, but we also know that many players will be on the go. There are some things that we are the best in the world to manufacture, and there are other things that will we partner on. So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this."

For now, anyone looking to play Wardogs will have to check out the PC version, which is currently in early access. Next week sees the launch of Season 2, which will introduce major gameplay features such as rain.

items.title: Wardogs' New Rain System Will Have a Major Effect on Gameplay in Season 2
items.description: Wardogs developer Bulkhead has revealed how rain will change the gameplay in Season 2.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Wardogs developer Bulkhead has revealed how rain will change the gameplay in Season 2.

Next week, Wardogs will release its second season of content, which will also add rain to the game. This will not be dynamic weather, so don't expect it to be sunshine one minute and storming the next; matches that include rain will experience rainfall the entire time, from start to finish. However, this will result in some major changes to the game, with senior producer Kane Allard confirming to IGN that it "completely changes the game," and as a result, some players may not actually like this addition.

"It completely changes the game, and it's going to be positive for some players," said Allard. "It's going to be negative for others. Your play styles might be affected. That's okay. It's not like every map's going to be permanently rain. It's just going to be almost like a different game mode, so to speak. [It] could be that some people really love rain, some people really hate rain based on how you want to play. But it does bring a lot."

As for how things change, it's pretty drastic. The map is obviously darker, and your visibility is worsened. One developer even stated that he lost his sense of direction on the map because he wasn't used to the way it looked now. The storms will cause thunder, which can be strategically used to mask gunfire or other loud noises. Raindrops will make different sounds based on the surfaces they're hitting, including rooftops and helmets. Windows will also fog up, though it's unclear if that allows players to be less visible when hiding in buildings. The team has also accounted for destruction, meaning if a roof is destroyed, players inside will be exposed to the rain.

As for other weather effects, Bulkhead isn't ruling anything out, but it has to consider how something like snow would change the game both in terms of gameplay and how the game performs. Bulkhead CEO Joe Brammer stated that there are obvious changes to something like nighttime, which would add flashlights, NVGs, and lasers. Maybe one day we'll get more, but it sounds like it may take some time to get added.

We've got plenty more on Wardogs, including Bulkhead on why blue team loses more, a new gambling mechanic for Season 2, and even word of a next-gen port. Wardogs Season 2 launches on October 15.

items.title: Wardogs Season 2 Adds a New Gambling Mechanic That Lets You Bet on Yourself
items.description: Wardogs Season 2 is adding a new gambling system which will allow players to bet on their own performance.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
Wardogs Season 2 is adding a new gambling system that will allow players to bet on their own performances.

The new season of Wardogs, due to launch on October 15, features a bunch of new content, most notably a new weather system that adds rain to matches. Another major mechanic lets players win big, or lose tons of cash. It's called the Wager Vendor, and it allows players to bet on themselves. If you think you can kill 20 people in a match, make a bet, and you will be rewarded. However, if you fail, you will lose cash. The harder your challenge is, the more you stand to win.

Speaking exclusively to IGN about the new system, developer Bulkhead noted that it technically won't be available to players as soon as the season launches, as they'll have to unlock it by building up cash.

"The Wager Vendor basically lets you bet on your own performance," said Bulkhead co-founder Howard Philpott. "So if I want to go in and say, 'I'm going to get 20 kills this match,' you then set that in your Wager Vendor, you then set the condition so I can say, 'Oh, I need to go and kill 20 people with my fists.' Okay, that's a bit harder, but that's when the odds go up. And then you set that as a condition and you can add multiple conditions."

"If you're a really good player and you're really smart about building your wager, you can make big money, but you can also lose big money," added senior producer Kane Allard.

Players can get pretty specific with these wagers. However, the more restrictions you put on yourself, the harder it will be to accomplish.

"Conditions-wise, it can even go down to as minute as, 'I need to get five kills, they're all head shots, all with the AK74M, and they all have to be in the hot zone, and my loadout has to cost less than 20K,'" said Allard. "You can build that wager and you can maybe earn double of what you put down, but that's a lot of restrictions that you're putting on yourself, and there's going to be players that may be also trying the same thing, and it just adds a little bit more tension to the game."

This not only spices up the gameplay, but it can also be extremely rewarding for players who are trying to build up some cash. If you're playing medic, you could theoretically give yourself a bonus for reviving 30 players. This then incentivizes medics to help their team more. It'll be intersting to see how this changes player behavior, but it sounds like it could be a lot of fun.

Call of Duty had a far less detailed version of this system in 2010's Call of Duty: Black Ops. Players could unlock items with an in-game currency and go into high stakes party games, such as Gun Game and One in the Chamber, to try and earn more money. GTA Online also has a betting system, allowing players to bet on players they think will perform best in PvP modes.

items.title: Battlefield 6’s Dead Space Event Has Players Storming Area 51
items.description: Battlefield 6 is getting a Dead Space event in time for Halloween. EA and Dice are calling it a “non-canon” event, which means the Battlefield 6 developer can go wild with it. Necromorphs in Area 51? Why not?
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Battlefield 6 is getting a Dead Space event in time for Halloween. EA and Dice are calling it a “non-canon” event, which means the Battlefield 6 developer can go wild with it. Necromorphs in Area 51? Why not?

The Dead Space and Battlefield 6 crossover was teased earlier in the week, with the alien monument The Marker showing up at the end of the shooter’s Vegas trailer. Pax Armata will be pursuing secret tech hidden beneath Area 51 in the event, which will be decked out with assets taken from the Dead Space remake.

Players will be able to unlock unique cosmetics for participating, starting when the event goes live on October 20. You’ll have until November 7 to grab what you want.

“Battlefield 6 is now one year old and what an incredible journey it’s been, from our Top Gun collaboration, which coincided with the return of Naval Warfare, to the launch of some of the most exhilarating maps in Battlefield history,” Battlefield Studios general manager Patrick Klaus said.

“And we’re just getting started, with Season 5 set to be the biggest yet. This has been an unforgettable year and we can’t thank players enough. We’re ending 2026 with a bang with three maps set in and around Las Vegas, a new way to experience REDSEC, as well as delivering on some of our community’s most requested features, with the introduction of Platoons and Server Browser. There’s never been a better time to play Battlefield.”

The new season sees players wage war across the Vegas strip, peppering the neon skyline with hot lead and baking under the desert sun. The area 51 map will also be playable across standard modes.

On November 10, another map will enter the rotation: European Casino. This close-quarters map will chew you up and spit you out like a real Vegas gambling den. Later, on December 8, Dice promises to “bring an unexpected chill” to Vegas, suggesting it’s about to get snowy in Sin City. Just go with it, it’s fine.

The REDSEC additions alluded to by Klaus come in the form of Rapid Royale, a fast-paced take on the battle royale across the Vegas Strip. Faster rounds, fewer players, and killing generates money you can spend on respawning back into the fight. This comes at the very start of the new season, which officially kicks off on October 13.

items.title: Peacemaker Taking a Backseat as James Gunn Builds Out the DCU, John Cena Says
items.description: John Cena said Peacemaker is taking a back seat as James Gunn focuses on building out the DCU with characters like Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
John Cena said Peacemaker is taking a back seat as James Gunn focuses on building out the DCU with characters like Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman.

The wrestler-turned-actor behind the Suicide Squad anti-hero opened up about the character's future during an interview on Happy, Sad, Confused. He said he's far from hung up Chris Smith's iconic metal helmet, but as for when he'll return as fans await Peacemaker Season 3, he can't say much.

"No," Cena said when asked if he's been in costume since the last episodes of his HBO show premiered in October of last year. "When I put that helmet on, I told James, I'm like, 'Dude, I'll put this helmet on as long as you need me to. He makes me a better performer, so I love being around him."

Cena was one of the first actors to work with Gunn when he began his transition to a new DC universe in 2019. Hot on the heels of his work with Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy, the filmmaker's work with DC was first limited to directing 2021's The Suicide Squad and, eventually, the Peacemaker TV show.

He's since become DC Studios co-CEO alongside Peter Safran and, as Paramount merges with Warner Bros., he's seemingly planted his roots at Skydance as DC Studios' co-chair. Like he's done so many times before, Gunn helped Peacemaker become a more recognizable face for fans, but Cena knows he's got more to worry about now.

After directing 2025's Superman, Gunn has returned to direct its sequel, Man of Tomorrow, which will premiere in 2027. In addition to his involvement in projects like Lanterns, Clayface, The Brave and the Bold, and more, the comic book movie overseer is also wrapped up looking to cast beloved icons like Batman and Wonder Woman. In other words, it's hard for watchers – and Cena – to pin down exactly when someone like Peacemaker might be able to return to the spotlight.

"Now, this dude gets to play with a whole box of toys, and because you get the whole box of toys, you have to address the really valuable ones first – and I understand that," Cena said. "So, here's a situation where I put my heart and soul into a character, an unknown character, and it becomes a fan favorite. I also know that it's OK. I gotta step back.

"Superman, Batman, Wonder Woman… There are so many valuable IPs. I'm not in a leadership spot, but if I was, I'd be making those plays first. That's OK."

Peacemaker received two seasons before leaving the status of Cena's Chris Smith on a major cliffhanger with Season 2. While there's been no word from Gunn on a Peacemaker Season 3, as the character's actor denies having put on the helmet since, it's hard to say we've seen the last of the character just yet.

Like Marvel's cinematic universe, the DCU feels ripe for experimentation when it comes to cameos and spinoffs. The Peacemaker character has already shown up for a live-action cameo in David Corenswet's first Superman movie, and while his status is somewhat unknown, it feels like he could always show up for more. As far as his overall arc his concerned, Cena said, at least as far as he's concerned, there's still "unfinished business."

"There always feels like unfinished business," he added. "I retired from wrestling, but people are like, 'Man, but you can come back!' You know what I'm saying? That's all that is to me: It's a message that, 'Dude, you did good work, and I'd like to see you again.' Nobody's saying, 'Good f**king riddance, Peacemaker. Bleh.'"

Gunn suggested Peacemaker Season 3 wasn't a priority late last year, saying, "Never say never, but right now, no." Addressing the Season 2 finale cliffhanger, he added, "This is about the future of the DCU." All of that said, the reflective-helmet-wearing character remains "really important" to the DC Studios boss as the DCU continues to come together.

We'll continue to see the pieces of his comic book movie universe fall into place when Clayface premieres later this month. Lanterns just introduced its Hal Jordan and John Stewart with Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre, but fans are already speculating about who might play characters like Wonder Woman and Batman. While we wait to see what's next for Peacemaker, you can check out IGN's 6/10 Season 2 finale review.

items.title: GTA 6 on Switch 2? 'That's a Conversation for Take-Two and Rockstar,' Nintendo Says
items.description: Will GTA 6 come out on Switch 2? The boss of Nintendo of America has responded.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Nintendo of America president Devon Pritchard recently spoke about the company's plans, from theme parks to first- and third-party games. And with the launch of Switch 2, the door is open to more third-party games that previously skipped Nintendo consoles (Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is one example). So what about GTA 6?

The Switch 2 is of course more powerful than its predecessor, capable of running games like Cyberpunk 2077 and the recent The Witcher 3 remaster. But could it run GTA 6? And, if so, will Rockstar Games release a Switch 2 port? After all, it's coming out on the less powerful Xbox Series S next month.

“That’s going to be a conversation for Take-Two and Rockstar, but nothing to announce on my end at this time,” Pritchard told Variety when asked about GTA 6 on Switch 2. Bah!

Rockstar games Red Dead Redemption, Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition, and L.A. Noire are already on Switch, but the developer hasn’t announced anything about Red Dead Redemption 2, never mind GTA 6. Would Manhunt be asking too much? Rockstar’s sequel, Manhunt 2, famously featured platform-specific controls for pummeling in heads with the motion controllers, and that’d work nicely on Switch 2 and make any onlookers afraid of taking me on when I play it on the train.

“We have historically said that Nintendo is for ages 5 to 95, and that continues to be true,” Pritchard said. “We want to provide a diversity in terms of the types of experiences that you can have on the game system, and that’s really important for us.”

Nintendo’s upcoming The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches on November 5, just two weeks before the launch of GTA 6. It’s about as close to Rockstar’s launch any triple-A game has dared, but Nintendo knows it has a captive audience of dedicated fans who love its stuff.

items.title: AI Driving Game Demo Forces Developer to Take Out Bank Loan to Keep It Running
items.description: The developer behind Teach My Little Sister How to Drive, a driving instruction sim where you instruct a generative-AI-powered, dynamic NPC, has been spending $1,000 dollars a day to keep the demo working.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
The developer behind Teach My Little Sister How to Drive, a driving instruction sim where you instruct a generative-AI-powered, dynamic NPC, has been spending $1,000 dollars a day to keep the demo working. “Over the past month, the number of demo players has grown more than twentyfold,” the developer said, via FRVR. “This growth has also increased our operating costs considerably.”

It all seems viable and a good business model so far. According to the blog post, developer Easy Fox had to take out a bank loan to support the game, which is powered by AI models. AI models costs can soar dramatically as the number of requests users make, which consume “tokens,” increase. Teach My Little Sister constantly queries AI as players interact with the game’s NPC to progress.

The developer plans to factor this in when deciding how much to charge for the game’s full release. “For the paid release, we plan to account for expected AI usage in the game’s price,” they said. “Players will not be charged separately for their individual AI token usage after purchasing the game. This isn’t because each player is particularly expensive to support. The total cost has increased because so many people are playing, and we have taken out a bank loan to help keep the demo running.

“We want to continue operating the demo and would love for more people to enjoy it. However, we are a small team of four, and financial pressure may mean we have to close the demo earlier than expected before the full release. We have not made that decision at this time.”

The game originally launched its demo in February, but interest from streamers such as thinknoodles has given it a popularity bump. The game is also popular in Asia, where there isn’t such a stigma around generative AI, which people in the West tend to hate because it’s a theft engine that sucks up the planet’s energy like Shinra.

Teach My Little Sister How to Drive relies on Google Gemini and ChatGPT to power its dynamic NPC, which follows your instructions, reacts, and disobeys, but the developers are looking into ways of allowing local AI models to step in for players “with sufficiently capable PCs.”

Companies making use of generative AI are starting to face reality. In a recent Axios report, one mystery company spent $500 million on AI tokens in a single month after failing to put usage limits on its account. Elsewhere, OpenClaw’s creator burned through $1.3 million in OpenAI API tokens in a single month.

There have been a few high profile instances of triple-A game developers either using generative AI or being caught up in the AI debate. Recently, Capcom had to clarify comments about its proprietary RE Engine being “AI powered.”

The publisher behind Arc Raiders came out in defense of AI use in Embark’s extraction shooter, but the team has since been making progress on replacing those stilted performances with human ones. Even games industry giant Activision has come under fire for AI usage in Call of Duty and its marketing materials.

items.title: YouTuber's Channel Permanently Banned Over Censored Hellraiser: Revival Gameplay Video
items.description: A YouTuber and streamer's channel was permanently banned for a Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival gameplay video.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
A YouTuber and streamer's channel was permanently banned for a Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival gameplay video.

French content creator J0nathan said that despite covering up the nudity in the game’s opening scenes with black boxes, his channel was removed for violating YouTube’s sex and nudity policy. “Explicit content that’s meant to be sexually gratifying isn’t allowed on YouTube,” the company told the streamer in response to an appeal upholding the ban.

Hellraiser: Revival, from Space Marine 2 developer Saber Interactive, opens with a raunchy sex scene featuring a topless woman and some BDSM play. Following that, the male character runs around for a while with their wang in the wind. While the scene is explicit, it’s essential to understanding the story and acts as the catalyst for everything that follows.

J0nathan claimed that this is the scene that got his channel banned, despite the fact uncensored gameplay of the same scene remains live on other YouTube channels. While he did add the "Not Made for Kids" label to the video, he did not age gate it, assuming that censoring the explicit scenes would be enough to satisfy YouTube.

"Since the rest of the game was just a standard horror title like Resident Evil I figured it didn't really require an age restriction, and that if anything, YouTube would just apply one later on like they always do," he said.

J0nathan had 190,000 subscribers on his channel at the time of the ban, which he told IGN was "permanent."

"My channel has been completely deleted, wiping out 10 years of hard work and destroying my main source of income," he continued. "I've never had any issues with the platform before. No warnings, no strikes, nothing. And yet they just threw me away like I was nothing.”

J0nathan said he has made attempts to run through YouTube’s appeal process, but “everything seems to be handled by AI.” His first appeal was rejected within a few minutes, and support accounts on social media responded with a generic message: "We've reviewed your case and are upholding our decision.”

“How can they possibly uphold such a decision when other videos showing the exact same scene without any censorship are still available on the platform?” he commented. “It really doesn't feel like any human being is actually reviewing these cases.”

J0nathan has a side channel but is afraid of using it because YouTube prohibits banned users from operating other channels. If he attempted it, he would run the risk of losing both channels. “I'm absolutely devastated,” he told IGN. “Beyond losing my income, I'm also losing 10 years of hard work and over 3,000 videos. The emotional impact is huge. Those videos represent a big part of my life, and losing them hurts more than I can describe.

“I've tried everything. I've reached out to my contacts, asked fellow content creators for help, but none of them have managed to get in touch with anyone at YouTube who could actually review my case. The same goes for the game developers. I've sent them emails and tagged them on X, hoping they might step in and help. I'm convinced they have contacts at YouTube to help prevent unfair bans related to their game, and yet they've completely ignored me.”

Ahead of Hellraiser's release, Saber tweeted to offer guidance to content creators concerned that their videos of the game would be at best demonetized, at worst get their channel deleted. Saber recommended content creators label all streams and videos with "appropriate age restrictions, sexual theme labels, and other necessary platform tools."

"You will need to adhere to each platform's community guidelines," Saber continued. There is no 'streamer mode,' Saber also pointed out on social media ahead of launch, "so context and intent behind your content will matter."

IGN has asked Saber Interactive for comment.
